findings.body: `reasoning_effort = "high"` sits at the gateway level alongside `scan`, `deep`, and `fallback`, so it applies to every model call — including the primary model `z-ai/glm-5.2`. The comment justifies the setting by saying it was "measured on `deepseek-v4-pro` at `high`" (a fallback model), and the earlier comment about glm-5.2's "5/5 clean runs" does not state whether those runs included reasoning. If glm-5.2 rejects `reasoning_effort` (the repo already contains error text `400: Extra inputs are not permitted: 'reasoning_effort'`) or consumes a large reasoning budget from the 8000-token `max_tokens`, the primary scan/deep calls will fail or degrade, pushing traffic to the more expensive fallbacks and negating the 40x cost savings the change is meant to deliver. The author should confirm that glm-5.2 was tested with `reasoning_effort = "high"` and report its reasoning token usage, or move the setting behind a per-model key if the consuming code supports that.
findings.title: Confirm reasoning_effort is validated for the primary model, not just fallback

value.summary: This config change swaps the OpenRouter gateway's scan and deep models to `z-ai/glm-5.2`, reworks the fallback chain, and introduces `reasoning_effort = "high"`. The primary concern is that the justification for the new reasoning setting is measured on a fallback model (`deepseek-v4-pro`), not the primary model (`glm-5.2`), and the setting applies at gateway level to every model call. If glm-5.2 does not support or behaves poorly with `reasoning_effort`, the primary path degrades and the cost savings are lost.
